correctness.rationale: For the continuum interval with generator (1/2)∂xx, the exact solution is the probability of hitting 0 before N by time t. The shortcut has strictly negative heat residual; the difference is the killed-heat evolution with positive forcing and zero boundary data. Starting the Duhamel formula at a positive time and letting that time decrease to zero justifies comparison despite the incompatible corner data: the bounded initial difference vanishes pointwise in the interior, and the residual is integrable at time zero. The reflection principle gives u≤ε_x and the strong Markov property gives ε_x−u≤ε_(2N−x), where ε_y=erfc(y/√(2t)). Indeed, dropping the order restriction on the first hit of N leaves two independent first-passage times across distances N−x and N; their Laplace transforms multiply to the transform across distance 2N−x. Substitution in v=(ε_x−ε_N)/(1−ε_N) gives the stated strict uniform upper bound. At x=N/2, ε_(2N−x)=o(ε_N) and ε_x→0 as t/N²→0, so the spatial supremum has asymptotic ε_N, without asserting a uniform pointwise equivalent. The numerical cutoff ratio is about 0.0046997190. Taylor division gives the positive 1/t coefficient x(N²−x²)/(6N), while the exact Dirichlet modes decay exponentially. Integrating the exact deficit gives −F''/2=1−x/N with zero endpoints, yielding the stated cubic, and the positive 1/t coefficient makes the shortcut integral diverge.
residual_risks: Only the stated continuum problem is reviewed; no finite-lattice error estimate or pointwise-equivalent error uniformly up to the endpoints follows.

value.rationale: The approximation is an actual published shortcut, so the error rather than a manufactured statistic is a motivated target. The result supplies a separation-independent tolerance and shows that its short-time scale cannot be improved even at a fixed bulk separation. The integrated comparison also identifies a concrete bias from extrapolating a convenient analytic form, rather than merely noting a visible mismatch.
residual_risks: The integrated diagnostic concerns extrapolation, not failure within the regime of good agreement, and does not address microscopic simulation accuracy.
